transcript.user_1_turn_1: This week somehow felt longer than the calendar says it was. I really want a quiet weekend.
transcript.user_2_turn_1: Sounds like your brain is already clocking out. Are you thinking mostly rest, or do you still have a bunch of weekend stuff to get through?
transcript.user_1_turn_2: A bit of both. I have errands Saturday morning and lunch with my sister Sunday. I was hoping to read in between.
transcript.user_2_turn_2: So probably something you can drop and pick back up without needing twenty minutes to remember what was happening.
transcript.user_1_turn_3: Yeah. I have The Glass Orchard, which is about 280 pages and supposed to be warm and a little weird, and Signal at Black Reef, which is a 430-page sci-fi mystery.
transcript.user_2_turn_3: Those are very different kinds of tired-weekend books.
transcript.user_1_turn_4: The annoying thing is Black Reef is a library copy due Monday. I've been waiting for it, but when I'm fried I can read the same plot-heavy page three times and still miss something.
transcript.user_2_turn_4: A due date can make a book feel urgent even when your attention span isn't volunteering.
transcript.user_1_turn_5: Exactly. Glass Orchard is mine, and my friend said it moves pretty quickly without introducing a million people.
transcript.user_2_turn_5: That sounds a lot easier to live with in short reading pockets.
transcript.user_1_turn_6: At this point I'm mostly picturing tea, rain on the window, and not turning Sunday night into another thing I have to finish.

That sounds like the perfect recipe for a quiet weekend: tea, the sound of rain, and a story that doesn't demand a detective's brain. Since *The Glass Orchard* is a quicker, warmer read, it might be the ideal companion for those rainy afternoons when you don't want to strain your eyes.

And if you have a bit of energy on Saturday, you could try to sneak in a chapter or two of *Black Reef* before your errands, but no pressure at all. You've already got a lot on your plate this week; let the books wait for you, not the other way around.
